eli5.text: This is a behind-the-scenes fix that makes the system less likely to accidentally add extra completion text in the wrong places. When processing streamed text, the code now checks whether the current text block actually starts with a tool-related tag before deciding to append the automatic finishing bit; previously it only checked if there was any text at all, which sometimes triggered the wrong behavior on non-tool content. This change is internal and does not affect what end users see or do.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task, it now sends a small summary message that shows the total cost of the work (in credits used), and if the assistant has a specific identity, that identifier is included too. This only shows up when you have the special "print mode" turned on, a setting some advanced users enable so the assistant outputs clean, machine-readable messages instead of the normal chat text. The cost number and any agent identity appear as a single line that other tools can easily read, while everyone else sees no difference from before. This is live today for anyone using print mode.

ai.title: Add baseAgent and subagents config to codebuff.json
ai.summary: Added optional `baseAgent` and `subagents` fields to `codebuff.json` schema, allowing explicit agent selection and subagent list override. Backend `main-prompt.ts` prioritizes config base agent over cost mode mapping, while `agent-registry.ts` uses configured subagents if present, replacing default base agent subagent lists. Covers `common/src/json-config` schema, `backend` agent resolution, and `npm-app` CLI display logic. Invalid base agent names throw errors listing available agents; subagents array completely replaces default plus custom agents when set.

eli5.text: When you run the coding assistant on a project, it used to pick which version of itself to use based only on a general setting like "fast" or "thorough". Now you can specify exactly which version you want by adding an entry to your project's configuration file, so the assistant always uses the one you chose instead of guessing from that general setting. If you list a set of helper tools in that same configuration, the assistant will use exactly those helpers instead of mixing in the default ones, which lets you keep out any helper you don't want running on your project. If you name a version that doesn't exist, the assistant will stop and tell you which versions are actually available rather than silently falling back. You would notice this the moment you start the assistant on a project

ai.title: Initial agent store schema
ai.summary: Added `agent_template` and `publisher` tables to the database schema. `agent_template` uses a composite primary key on `id` and `version`, with generated columns for semantic versioning parts. `publisher` enforces unique `slug` and links to templates via `publisher_id` foreign key. Migration `0022_whole_juggernaut.sql` and corresponding Drizzle snapshot updated.

eli5.text: You (or your organization) can now publish and install agent templates through a new built-in store. The system now remembers who published each template and keeps a unique name (slug) for each publisher, so you can install the same agent name from different publishers without collisions. Behind the scenes, versions like 1.2.3 are stored as major (1), minor (2), and patch (3) so filtering and updates work cleanly. Note this change is live in the database schema today, but no templates or publishers are visible in the store until someone actually adds them. Existing behavior is unaffected until content is submitted.

This means any custom helper files placed anywhere within that folder are automatically picked up and made available to you, rather than needing to live in one specific location. The older, rigid folder structure has been removed, so you can now freely arrange your helper files in nested groups.

eli5.text: Nothing about your experience actually changed today. The team simply tagged the software with a new internal version number and bundled in a collection of small, already-in-place capabilities from the past day. One of those capabilities lets the assistant report how much an action cost once it finishes, another lets teams define helper sub-agents through configuration, and a couple of others make agent templates load more flexibly and give them better built-in documentation. Because the version-label itself only repackages existing work rather than flipping on new behavior, you wouldn't notice anything different by simply updating.

eli5.text: When the assistant receives a tool call with malformed or unrecognized formatting, the system now records detailed diagnostic information including the specific error type, message, and where it occurred. This improved logging helps developers identify and fix parsing problems faster. Affected components include backend analytics events and XML stream parsing functionality. No immediate user-facing behavior changes, but debugging becomes more efficient.

ai.title: dynamic-agent-template schema aligned with AgentConfig
ai.summary: DynamicAgentConfigSchema in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts updated to match AgentConfig. JsonSchemaSchema replaced with recursive z.lazy definition supporting nested properties. toolNames, subagents, and prompt fields made optional with defaults adjusted. Added _typecheck assertion enforcing AgentConfig compatibility.

eli5.text: You define an agent using a template file, and that file can now leave out several fields that used to be required, including the system, instructions, and step prompts, as well as the list of tools the agent is allowed to use. Where a field is left blank, the system fills in a sensible default instead of rejecting the file, so a minimal agent definition can be as short as an id plus a step prompt. The template now also accepts nested parameter shapes (objects inside objects) for input and output, matching the richer format the rest of the system already uses, and a behind-the-scenes check makes sure the two formats stay compatible going forward. Nothing in the agent’s finished behavior changes right now; this just makes the template format easier to write and keep in sync.

eli5.text: The assistant's step-by-step process is now checked upfront to make sure it follows the right pattern (a generator function), so misconfigured assistants get caught before they run. The labels for the assistant's working memory moved to a simpler format in the background definitions, and the settings that define an assistant were rearranged into neat groups (tools first, then how it talks, then its instructions) without changing how anything works. This is live today and won't change what you see on screen.

ai.title: Simplify agent builder prompts and default includeMessageHistory
ai.summary: Agent builder system prompts now enforce minimal fields and concise instructions, removing redundant stepPrompt content. The `includeMessageHistory` flag defaults to `false` in `AgentConfig`, requiring explicit opt-in for context preservation. Updated type definitions in `common/src/templates/agent-template.d.ts` clarify `parentPrompt` usage for subagents and refine `inputSchema` guidance. These changes reduce template complexity and align agent behavior with smart model capabilities.

ai.title: Remove parentInstructions from agent templates
ai.summary: Soft-removed parentInstructions from agent templates by stripping it from AgentConfig interface and prompt instructions in agent-builder.ts. Field retained as optional in DynamicAgentConfigSchema for backward compatibility, marked for potential full removal.

eli5.text: The system used to ask builders of custom assistant templates to include guidance telling parent assistants when to activate those assistants. That guidance field has now been dropped from the main template setup, so new templates no longer need to fill it in. The field is kept around quietly for older templates that still use it, so nothing that already exists breaks. If you're creating a new custom assistant from a template, you'll simply notice that the instructions for parent assistants are no longer part of the required setup.

ai.title: Dynamic agent template schema drops handleSteps generator check
ai.summary: Removed Zod refine enforcing GeneratorFunction on handleSteps in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts. Upstream generator-name check broke under minification/transpile. AgentConfig docs in .agents/agent-template.d.ts clarify parentPrompt, systemPrompt, stepPrompt, inputSchema, and includeMessageHistory defaults. Scope limited to shared core types and template typings.

eli5.text: Templates that define reusable AI assistants no longer enforce a strict check on a part of the template that was being validated as a special kind of function. Minifiers and code transformers were rewriting that piece in a way that broke the check, so the system would reject otherwise valid templates. The validation is gone, so templates will load reliably again after being processed. Live today for anyone building custom assistants from shared templates.

ai.title: Rename agent-template to agent-config
ai.summary: Renamed agent-template.d.ts to agent-config.d.ts across shared types, CLI agents, and backend builder. Updated imports in brainstormer, git-committer, and knowledge-keeper. Added AGENT_CONFIG_FILE constant to common/src/constants.ts. Backend agent-builder now dynamically resolves template path via this constant.

eli5.text: The system renamed a behind-the-scenes configuration file from agent-template to agent-config across several parts of the codebase. If you looked, you would see fewer scattered references to the old file name and one central place where the new name is defined. This affects only people building custom assistants on top of the platform, and the practical behavior of any assistant you are already using today does not change.

ai.title: New Charles agent config
ai.summary: Added .agents/charles.ts defining Charles, a deep sea sardine research specialist. Configures model anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522 with web_search, read_docs, write_file, read_files, spawn_agents, end_turn tools. Subagents researcher and thinker handle specialized tasks. System prompt scopes expertise to sardine biology, ecology, and conservation.

eli5.text: A new specialized research assistant named Charles has been added to the company's internal tool kit. Charles is specifically designed to answer detailed questions about deep sea sardines and marine biology. If you're an internal researcher or team member looking up information on sardine behavior, migration patterns, ocean conditions, or conservation efforts, Charles can now be summoned to gather and summarize scientific sources, using web searches and document review tools. This capability is now available within the internal tooling environment.

ai.title: Comment out parentInstructions in knowledge-keeper
ai.summary: The `parentInstructions` object in `.agents/knowledge-keeper.ts` is commented out, disabling automatic subagent spawning directives for researcher, file_picker, reviewer, thinker, brainstormer, base, and planner. This change is internal to the agent configuration and does not affect user-facing functionality directly. The `subagents` array remains active, preserving the list of available subagents.

eli5.text: The project's documentation assistant used to automatically decide to bring in a specialized helper whenever certain conditions arose, like finding a new config file, spotting outdated docs during a review, or finishing a brainstorming session. That automatic decision-making has now been turned off; the helper instructions are still written down but are ignored. The specialized helper is still available if needed manually, but it will no longer be pulled in on its own based on what's happening in the project. This only affects the internal setup of the documentation assistant and won't change anything you see or do directly.

ai.title: Refactor git-committer agent config
ai.summary: Removed unused `ToolResult` and `ToolCall` imports from `.agents/git-committer.ts`. Consolidated `parentInstructions.base` text into `parentPrompt` and deleted the redundant `parentInstructions` object. No runtime behavior change for git commit agent.

eli5.text: The git committer agent's configuration was cleaned up by removing unused settings and combining duplicate instructions into one place. If you looked at the configuration, you would see fewer lines of text and no leftover or repeated phrases. This is a behind-the-scenes change that does not affect how the agent works, and it is live today as part of the current version of the software.

ai.title: Dynamic agent template schema fixes
ai.summary: AgentConfig import switched from templates/agent-template to util/agent-config. InputSchemaObjectSchema.prompt now uses .passthrough() to allow extra keys. Fixes test failures in dynamic-agent-loader and dynamic-agent-schema-validation.

eli5.text: A bug that was making the system reject agent templates with unexpected extra options has been resolved, so templates that include additional configuration fields now load correctly again. This fixes the failures in the automated checks that verify agent templates load and validate their schema, which had been stopping recent test runs from passing. The change is live today in the backend and common packages.

ai.title: CI parallel typecheck and web build fail-fast
ai.summary: CI workflow now executes `bun run typecheck` and `bun run build` (in `web/`) via `Promise.all` instead of shell background jobs. This ensures immediate failure propagation and proper exit code handling if either process errors. Change is scoped to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: When the project runs its automated checks, it now starts the error-checking and website-building steps at the same time using a more reliable coordination method. If either step fails, the whole check stops immediately instead of continuing. You wouldn't see anything different unless one of those steps broke, in which case the failure shows up sooner and more clearly than before.

ai.title: ci.yml parallel typecheck and build
ai.summary: Removed `timeout` wrapper and replaced `wait` with explicit `wait $PID1 && wait $PID2` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Ensures CI fails if either typecheck or build fails, fixing silent error swallowing. Applies to Web CI jobs.

eli5.text: When the web project's test-and-build process runs, it now actually catches failures instead of letting them slip through silently. Previously, the system ran two checks at the same time but used a loose waiting method that could ignore if one failed. Now it waits for each check explicitly, so if either the type-checking or the build breaks, the whole process stops and reports the error. This affects anyone running or relying on the web CI jobs, which are now more reliable.

eli5.text: The assistant software was given a new internal version number, which is what gets published and installed by users. When you update to this version, you gain a few behind-the-scenes improvements: the assistant now handles slightly more reliable configuration settings for its helper modules, logs failed tool calls in a more readable way for developers to debug, and checks its own work more carefully when building new configurations. A couple of small cleanups were also made to remove outdated instructions from templates, keeping things tidy for future updates. This update went live on July 29, 2025.

ai.title: Enforce NOT NULL constraint on agenttemplate and publisher id columns
ai.summary: Migration 0022 updates `agent_template.id` to enforce `NOT NULL`, aligning with `publisher.id` changes in schema.ts. This fixes local database integrity issues where ID columns previously allowed null values despite using `crypto.randomUUID()` defaults. The change modifies `common/src/db/schema.ts`, `0022_graceful_titanium_man.sql`, and associated metadata snapshots.

eli5.text: The software no longer accepts entries in its local storage where the identifier field is left blank, previously it would save a record with an empty ID even though it was supposed to generate one automatically, and now it requires that ID to actually exist. This only affects the local database used during development and testing, not any production system or live feature. The developer who reported this was able to reproduce integrity issues locally, and this fix closes that gap. No visible behavior changes for end users; the system just stores its own records more reliably now.
